corrections.critique: Strongest feature: O'Connor anchors the transmission challenge in manuscript phenomena, particularly Mark's discrepant endings, then advances the proportionate inference that comparable reshaping during undocumented oral circulation remains plausible. Principal limitation: Observable postcomposition interpolation does not establish precomposition alteration, and the argument underdevelops whether identification of late variants evidences textual comparison, circumscribed contamination, or generalized unreliability. Live burden: D'Souza must explain why recoverable written editing provides little evidential purchase on less recoverable oral development, while O'Connor must connect possibility to meaningful probability without treating every tradition as equally unstable. Locked score: The very strong 85–94 band appropriately reflects a precise, centrally relevant evidential challenge whose calibrated modal conclusion survives, notwithstanding an inferential bridge that remains suggestive rather than demonstrative.
